title: Find Proteins of Unknown Function (PUFs) using Plantannot - Protocol A
author: Marcos Viana
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgcvjsw6

steps.title: Open Plantannot search page
steps.instruction: Navigate to https://www.machado.cnptia.embrapa.br/plantannot/find/?q= (or open the Plantannot home page and click the magnifying‑glass icon) ensuring the search box is empty, then load the page with empty filters.

steps.title: Select organism filter
steps.instruction: In the left “Filters” card, expand the “Organisms” section using the green arrow, choose the desired organism(s) (e.g., Oropetium thomaeum) or leave all boxes unchecked to include all organisms, and click “Apply”.

steps.title: Choose feature type
steps.instruction: In the “Feature type” filter, check the box for “polypeptide” and click “Apply”.

steps.title: Set analyses filters
steps.instruction: In the “Analyses” filter, check both “no diamond matches” and “no interproscan matches”, then click “Apply”.

steps.title: Leave other filters empty
steps.instruction: Ensure the “Orthology”, “Coexpression”, and “Orthologs_coexpression” filters remain unchecked (empty).

steps.title: View and download results
steps.instruction: After applying all filters, the “Results” card on the center‑right will show the filtered list (e.g., 2,541 PUFs for Oropetium thomaeum). By default 50 entries are displayed; you can change this number at the bottom of the page or navigate through pages. Click the highlighted download icon at the top‑right of the results pane to export the complete list as a .tsv file.
